features.name: AI code generation for legacy AL refactoring
features.description: Using AI agents to assist in refactoring and improving legacy AL code that may have been ported from older versions. AI is good at understanding test-driven development principles and writing tests quickly, but produces non-deterministic code that can fail.
caveats: AI-generated code is non-deterministic and may fail
AI behavior changes almost weekly as new models are released
Difficult to generate tests for very long legacy procedures with complex logic

features.name: Compilation as first-pass validation for AI agents
features.description: Using compilation checks as a feedback loop to ensure AI-generated code compiles before further validation. This is the basic first check any developer performs.

features.name: Static analysis linters for code quality
features.description: Using Microsoft's AppSource Cop, Pertenent Cop, Code Cop, and UI Cop linters, plus community linters, to provide feedback on code quality. Recommends linters that check code complexity to prevent AI from writing overly long procedures.
caveats: Some community linters are deprecated in favor of new ones

features.name: Complexity linters for procedure length control
features.description: Linters focused on code complexity that prevent AI agents from writing long, complicated procedures by triggering compiler errors when complexity thresholds are exceeded.

features.name: Warning-as-errors compiler option with ruleset files
features.description: Using a compiler option to treat all warnings as errors, combined with a ruleset file to define which issues are errors vs warnings. This creates a black-and-white approach where code either compiles or it doesn't.
caveats: Requires discipline to avoid agents concluding warnings are unimportant after repeated failures

features.name: Test-driven development with AI agents
features.description: Using automated test suites to enable AI agents to perform full loops of writing tests, seeing them fail, writing production code, and refactoring. Requires upfront planning and a test plan. Agents can write tests, run code, verify failures, write implementations, and execute refactoring in full loops before returning to the user.
caveats: Requires upfront planning and test plan definition
Requires modern, optimized test code for AI to write correct tests easily
Requires build automation infrastructure

features.name: Build automation and CI/CD for agent loops
features.description: Using GitHub or DevOps CI/CD pipelines to run automated tests as part of the build process, layered on top of automated tests in the agent development loop.

features.name: Debug logging via telemetry interception
features.description: A pattern using AL's standard telemetry logger interface to intercept feature telemetry calls and write them to JSONL files inside Docker containers, making execution paths immediately visible to agents without file system access delays. Debug logs inserted into conditional branches verify which code paths execute during test runs, automating what was previously manual breakpoint debugging.
caveats: Standard Application Insights approach has 2-5 minute delays
Works asynchronously and may write to individual files that must be combined
Not blocking to code execution

features.name: Observational test patterns for code discovery
features.description: Tests that observe and record which code paths are actually executed in legacy procedures without asserting correctness. These tests capture the existing behavior before refactoring, allowing agents to detect test setup issues or unexpected path execution.
caveats: Do not assert correctness of the code
Should pass existing bugs before refactoring
Used specifically for legacy code refactoring

features.name: Automated path coverage verification
features.description: A technique to inject logging commands into all if statements and cases within a procedure, allowing tests to automatically verify which code paths are actually executed. This replaces manual debugging with breakpoints.
caveats: Requires manual code instrumentation or agent assistance
Must be done before or during test execution

features.name: Approval testing for refactoring preparation
features.description: Tests that observe existing code behavior before refactoring, allowing bugs to pass initially so that refactoring can proceed one-to-one without fixing unrelated issues. These kinds of tests do not say anything about whether the code is doing the right thing.
caveats: purpose is to capture existing behavior, not validate correctness
bugs pass initially by design

features.name: Mutation testing for scenario coverage verification
features.description: Systematically mutate one production code element at a time to verify tests fail appropriately, ensuring all scenarios are actually tested rather than relying on execution logs.
caveats: slower feedback than debug logs
requires reverting changes after each test
time-consuming but can be automated with agents

features.name: Test-driven development loop in refactoring
features.description: After approval tests establish baseline behavior, apply TDD loop by writing new test first without implementation, then adding minimal logic to pass, then refactoring to clean code.

features.name: Wrapper procedures for safe refactoring
features.description: Create wrapper procedures with identical signatures to original implementations, routing calls to either old or new implementation, enabling same approval tests to validate both versions pass identically.
caveats: requires exact interface and signature matching
test must pass on both old and new implementations

features.name: Agent-assisted economics of safe refactoring
features.description: AI agents make safe refactoring economically viable by automating repetitive testing and mutation validation work, enabling clean code improvements that subsequently unlock greater agent productivity.
caveats: real value emerges through cascading productivity gains
clean code prerequisite for effective agent use

features.name: Large language model selection for AL code
features.description: Advanced models like Claude Opus and DBT55 follow prompt instructions reliably for AL development tasks without requiring additional constraint hooks.
caveats: these models are expensive
nondeterministic behavior requires careful prompt engineering

features.name: Git hooks for agent instruction enforcement
features.description: Use git hooks or coding agent hooks to enforce script execution at specific points, such as requiring test runs before returning code to user.
caveats: presenter uses prompt instructions instead in current workflow
hooks approach less relied upon with modern LLMs

features.name: Tests as project documentation for agents
features.description: Test suites serve as faster-to-read documentation of project behavior expectations compared to implementation code, helping AI agents understand intended functionality more efficiently.

features.name: AI Agent for test execution and verification
features.description: Using AI agents to run tests and ensure test execution before returning to users, replacing previous hook-based approaches with skills. Works with large projects.
caveats: works for the speaker's large projects

features.name: Leave codebase better rule
features.description: Refactoring principle where developers must leave the codebase better than they found it, even if only adding three tests and refactoring a simple procedure.

features.name: Touch code only when necessary
features.description: General rule to not touch code that works; changes should only be made when actively working on that part, combined with efforts to improve it.

features.name: AI-assisted test development playbook
features.description: Recommended workflow: pick familiar code, add tests (possibly test-driven), ask AI about testing, consult Microsoft Learn and agent documentation, characterize, prove and refactor.
caveats: AI models don't fully know AL test framework

features.name: Debug logging with feature telemetry safety nets
features.description: Using debug logging markers in code during refactoring with AI agents, with CI/CD checks and safety nets to ensure these markers are removed before shipping.
caveats: markers must be removed before shipping
timing depends on refactor size

features.name: AI-generated mutation testing plans
features.description: AI agents create mutation testing plans by suggesting code changes like modifying if statements or assignments. Developer reviews plan before agent executes mutations, compiles, publishes and runs tests.
caveats: mutation testing is time-consuming across languages
requires compile, publish, test, revert cycle

features.name: Characterization testing for legacy code
features.description: Temporary tests that assert behavior of legacy code to allow switching over to new refactored code. These tests are removed after refactoring completes as they require heavy setup and database access.
caveats: slow to run
require database access and commits
intended to be temporary

features.name: Real unit and integration tests after refactoring
features.description: After characterization phase, build proper unit and integration tests based on knowledge gained from characterization tests and AI assistance, with normal test coverage.

features.name: Bug discovery during decoupling and refactoring
features.description: When decoupling legacy codebase and writing tests for new code, developers recognize bugs in the legacy codebase that can be fixed after refactoring is complete.
caveats: bugs only fixed after refactoring complete
